issues: As correctly noted in the script's comments, numerous performance-critical process placement and binding options from the original `jsrun` command (e.g., `-r6`, `-brs`, `--smpiargs="-gpu"`) were omitted. For an extremely large-scale (3600 tasks, 3600 GPUs) tightly-coupled MPI application, the lack of explicit process placement control can lead to sub-optimal NUMA locality and network communication patterns, potentially causing catastrophic performance degradation.

The script is missing an explicit memory request. The original LSF script also omitted this. For a job of this magnitude, this is a catastrophic omission. The job will receive a small, default memory allocation and is almost certain to fail with out-of-memory errors.

The script is extremely non-portable. It uses the `$HOME` variable to construct an absolute path and also contains other hardcoded absolute paths. It will fail for any user other than the original author.
